title: Regional failover automation upgrade — project notes (working doc)
content:
Owner: Rafael (SRE)
Maintainers: Miles (design/arch), Aisha (SLO + alerting), Tomáš (runbook), Peter (embedded SRE w/ Routing)
Last “big” review: 2025-05-06 (post low-risk prod test + threshold tuning)

Purpose of this doc
- Working scratchpad for the regional failover automation upgrade.
- Weekly notes + open questions, rough thresholds, action items.
- This is not the final spec/ADR — see Confluence for cleaned-up versions.

Quick links
- Program overview (Confluence): /eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/regional-failover-automation-upgrade-overview
- ADR-0247 (Confluence): /architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0247-failover-trigger-engine-and-safety-guards
- Runbook (Confluence): /oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/automated-region-failover-runbook
- Dashboard spec (Confluence): /eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/failover-dashboards-and-alerts-spec
- Game day plan (Confluence): /oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/controlled-failover-game-day-plan-2025q2

Implementation pointers
- Trigger module PR: redwood#98231
- Orchestrator state machine + audit PR: redwood#98248
- Progressive failover PR: redwood#98277
- Safe-to-failover checks PR: redwood#98305
- Degradation controls PR: redwood#98322
- Dashboards/alerts PR: observability-pack#441
- Incident bot PR: incident-bot#188
- Perf canary scenario PR: perf-canary#267
- Terraform routing/DNS primitives PR: redwood-terraform#913
- Helm wiring PR: redwood-helm-charts#522
- Burn-rate correlations PR: slo-toolkit#301
- Hold-down + rollback integration tests PR: redwood#98390
- Signal ingestion wiring PR: redwood#98412

Glossary (informal)
- “Trigger engine” = evaluates region health signals against rules (thresholds/windows/hysteresis) -> emits “degraded” / “failed” / “recovering” recommendations.
- “Orchestrator” = state machine that actually changes routing/DNS/policy (progressive) once safe-to-failover checks pass.
- “Monitor-only mode” = triggers compute recommendations + audit log, but orchestration does not change production routing.
- “Progressive failover” = apply failover to a controlled slice first (by % / by tier / by route/model).

Current status (as of 2025-05-07)
- Trigger evaluation + orchestrator implemented behind feature flag; monitor-only proven useful in 1 small real incident (see Slack #incidents 1715176602).
- Staging game day completed; follow-ups mostly around signal noise + dashboard clarity.
- Production controlled failover executed for low-risk segment; net impact acceptable, but learned:
  - DNS propagation is not the limiting factor (internal policy flip is), but edge caches still introduce non-trivial tail (need better visibility on “where did request route?”).
  - Capacity headroom checks were too optimistic for one GPU pool (queue depth spiked after failover; safe-to-failover checks must incorporate “expected added load” not just current free).
  - Burn alerts were too chatty on “degraded but available” (tune paging thresholds + add non-paging warnings).

Open questions (living)
1) What’s our canonical “region health” for decisioning?
   - Current: combine request success rate + tail latency + synthetic probes + dependency health + capacity saturation.
   - Open: do we weight customer-impact metrics higher than synthetic? (tendency: yes)
   - Open: how do we avoid synthetic-probe false positives (ISP/localized network) from flipping region state?

2) Progressive failover slicing rules
   - Should we default slice by customer tier (free/self-serve -> lowest risk, enterprise dedicated -> highest risk)?
   - Do we need an explicit per-customer “allowed target regions” list (data residency) enforced at orchestrator level?
   - Mina’s concern (Routing): policy complexity explosion. Proposed mitigation: orchestrator supports 2–3 first-class primitives only:
     a) percentage
     b) tier scope
     c) route/model scope

3) Safe-to-failover checks (capacity + dependencies)
   - What’s authoritative capacity? Harish/Vanessa say fleet signals can lag a few minutes during fast churn.
   - Need to settle on: GPU headroom %, queue depth, and “expected incremental load” approximation.
   - Networking dependencies: if cross-region link is impaired, failing over may worsen tail latency vs staying put.

4) How do we represent “degraded but available” vs “failed” in routing policy?
   - Degraded state should bias routing away for best-effort traffic, but not necessarily evacuate enterprise pinned customers.
   - Need clear runbook language: “degraded triggers load shed + timeouts + variant fallback” before full failover.

5) Manual override + audit
   - Who can force failover? Who can block? (INT-881 tracks RBAC adjustments)
   - Audit log retention + where it’s visible (Console vs logs vs Confluence export).

Draft signal contract (rough, evolves) — ENG-2842
All signals should be published per region, per “service slice” (Hosted API vs Dedicated pools where applicable), and be queryable with a consistent time window.

Required region health indicators (MVP)
- Customer-impact metrics
  - api.request_success_rate (1 - (5xx + 429? + timeouts))
  - api.p99_latency_ms (and optionally p95)
  - streaming.disconnect_rate
- Dependency metrics
  - kv_store.error_rate (routing policy store)
  - auth/token_service.error_rate (if customer auth is regional)
  - object_store/weights_fetch (mostly startup, but impacts scaling)
- Capacity saturation
  - gpu_pool.utilization
  - gpu_pool.available_tokens_per_sec headroom estimate (or effective throughput)
  - queue.depth + queue.wait_p99
- Network path health
  - synthetic_probes.http_success_rate (from multiple vantage points)
  - packet_loss / tcp_connect_time to region ingress

Notes
- We agreed (Slack eng-infra 1711559201) probes must run from:
  - at least 2 cloud regions outside the target region
  - at least 1 in-region vantage point (to detect ingress-only issues)
  - ideally 1 “public internet” path and 1 “cloud backbone” path

Draft thresholds (INITIAL / SUBJECT TO TUNING)
These are starting points. Do not treat as commitments.

Terminology
- “window” = evaluation window
- “hold-down” = minimum time to remain in a state before allowing reversal
- “hysteresis” = require stronger evidence to flip back to healthy than to become unhealthy

A) Enter DEGRADED (candidate)
- Trigger A1 (tail latency): api.p99_latency_ms > 2,500ms for 5m AND request volume > baseline_min
- Trigger A2 (error rate): api.5xx_rate > 1.5% for 5m AND api.rps > baseline_min
- Trigger A3 (streaming): streaming.disconnect_rate > 0.8% for 10m (only for streaming-enabled routes)
- Trigger A4 (network): synthetic_probes.http_success_rate < 98.5% for 5m from >=2 vantage points

DEGRADED actions (automation)
- Do NOT automatically fail over by default.
- Enable graceful degradation controls:
  - tighten timeouts for best-effort tiers (avoid queue pileup)
  - enable controlled load shedding for non-enterprise traffic
  - prefer fallback model variants if primary model backend is saturated

B) Enter FAILED (candidate for failover)
- Trigger B1 (hard errors): api.5xx_rate > 5% for 2m OR > 3% for 5m
- Trigger B2 (unavailable): synthetic_probes.http_success_rate < 95% for 2m from >=2 vantage points
- Trigger B3 (latency collapse): api.p99_latency_ms > 8,000ms for 3m + queue.wait_p99 > 5,000ms

FAILED -> Failover prerequisites (safe-to-failover checks)
- Target region “healthy enough”
  - target api.5xx_rate < 1% for 10m
  - target p99 < 2,500ms for 10m
- Capacity headroom
  - target gpu_pool.utilization < 80% (or headroom >= 20%) for 10m
  - AND estimated added load fits under headroom with 1.2x safety factor
  - AND queue.depth stable (not increasing) for 10m
- Dependency gating
  - routing policy store healthy in target
  - cross-region connectivity between edge/router and target region not impaired (packet loss < 1% over 5m)

Hold-down timers / flappiness controls
- DEGRADED hold-down: 15m minimum
- FAILED hold-down: 30m minimum
- Recovery hysteresis: require 2x longer healthy window than unhealthy detection window to exit state

Progressive failover policy (proposal)
- Step 0: monitor-only (no routing changes) — current default in prod until we expand
- Step 1: canary % for lowest-risk routes
  - 5% traffic for 10m
  - then 25% for 10m
  - then 50% (optional)
  - then 100% if needed
- Step 2: widen by tier and route/model
  - do NOT include enterprise pinned/dedicated unless explicitly enabled for that customer/pool

What counts as “stop condition” during progressive failover
- Target region’s p99 increases above 3,500ms for >3m
- Target 5xx_rate exceeds 1.5% for >3m
- Queue depth rising monotonically for >5m
- Customer-visible SLO burn crosses “fast burn” threshold (see Aisha notes below)

Observability / dashboard notes (Sergio + Felix)
- We need a single “state timeline” view per region:
  - signal summaries
  - trigger engine recommendation
  - orchestrator state (monitor-only vs active)
  - progressive stage (5%/25%/100%)
  - manual override events
- “Customer impact by tier” must be front-and-center for IC decisions.
- Add explicit panels for:
  - request volume shift by region
  - cross-region latency
  - queue wait times and dropped requests from load shedding

SLO + alerting notes (Aisha)
- Goal: align alerts with multi-window multi-burn and make failover actions auditable against error budget.
- Proposed categories:
  1) Paging (fast burn): likely customer-visible, action needed now
  2) Ticket/Warning: early signal, may be noisy, but useful for trigger engine
- IMPORTANT: do not page on “synthetic probes only” without a customer-impact corroboration.
- Burn alerts should include links:
  - “what state is orchestrator in?”
  - “are we in progressive failover?”
  - “safe-to-failover checks passing?”

Runbook edits needed (Tomáš)
- Clarify the decision tree:
  - degraded -> apply degradation controls
  - failed -> progressive failover (if safe)
  - when to force manual override
- Add explicit verification steps post-action:
  - confirm routing distribution has moved as expected
  - confirm SLO burn slows within 10–15m
  - confirm queue drain
  - confirm target region capacity stable

Infra / DNS / edge routing notes (Irene + Victor)
- DNS TTL strategy for controlled tests:
  - keep conservative defaults (avoid global whiplash)
  - rely more on internal routing policy changes than external DNS flips for progressive steps
- Change windows:
  - infra requires review + scheduled change window for terraform modules that touch edge
  - game day must include explicit rollback plan and “break glass” contacts

Weekly notes

Week of 2025-01-27
- Kickoff. Reviewed last 2 regional incidents (see incident synthesis in Confluence incident review doc).
- Primary recurring issue: detection + decision lag, and uncertainty about “is target region safe?”
- Action items:
  - Miles: draft state machine and triggers (starting point)
  - Peter + Mina: list routing surfaces that can be changed progressively
  - Irene + Victor: outline DNS/edge levers vs internal policy levers

Week of 2025-02-03
- Signal inventory:
  - Some regions have good p99, but missing streaming disconnects in a consistent metric name.
  - Capacity signals inconsistent between Hosted and Dedicated pools.
- Decisions (tentative):
  - Build central aggregator (ENG-2843) rather than per-service triggers.
  - Publish a region_health summary object (even if we store as individual time series).
- Open question: Do we treat 429 as a “failure” for failover triggers? leaning: no (it’s often intentional); but it should contribute to “degraded” user experience.

Week of 2025-02-10
- Draft thresholds v0 shared in Slack eng-sre 1711392105.
- Flappiness concerns raised:
  - Need hysteresis/hold-down as first-class config.
  - Add “manual override required” for first production stage.
- Email approval thread started for staging game day scope (Neha/Sean/Priya).

Week of 2025-02-17
- Routing team feedback:
  - Progressive failover must be gated by feature flag and constrained primitives.
  - They want clear acceptance criteria: “rollback at any stage in < 2 minutes.”
- Infra feedback:
  - Synthetic probes caused false positives previously; must correlate.
- Action items:
  - Jordan: implement trigger engine config schema w/ windows/hysteresis (redwood#98231)
  - Ethan: define orchestrator API shape + audit events (redwood#98248)

Week of 2025-02-24
- Safe-to-failover concept refined:
  - Not just “target capacity now,” but “target capacity after we move X% traffic.”
  - Proposed: estimate added tokens/sec from source region + recent load.
- Drafted stop conditions for game day.
- Dashboard mock notes started (separate doc in Observability drive).

Week of 2025-03-03
- Release gating discussion w/ Connor (email thread: feature flag rollout stages).
- Agreement:
  - Stage 1 in prod = monitor-only (audit + incident-bot notices, but no changes)
  - Stage 2 = enable progressive failover for a low-risk route + free/self-serve tier only
  - Stage 3 = expand coverage by route/model; enterprise only with explicit approval

Week of 2025-03-10
- Observability PR created (observability-pack#441)
- Incident bot integration started (incident-bot#188)
- Runbook outline in progress; needs screenshots once dashboards are stable.

Week of 2025-03-17
- Safe-to-failover checks PR in review (redwood#98305)
- Debate: capacity headroom threshold
  - Harish: 20% may be insufficient in practice due to burstiness
  - Peter: too high makes failover “never happen”
  - Compromise: 20% baseline + require queue depth stable + apply safety factor to estimated added load.

Week of 2025-03-24 (staging game day)
- Executed staging impairment scenario: elevated 5xx + latency.
- What worked:
  - Trigger engine correctly flagged DEGRADED within ~4m.
  - Orchestrator state transitions logged and visible.
- Issues:
  - Synthetic probes flagged FAILED earlier than customer metrics (false positive due to one vantage point)
  - Dashboard “state” panel unclear (recommendation vs actual)
  - One alert paged SRE even though impact contained in staging (fix routing labels)
- Follow-ups:
  - require >=2 vantage points for probe-based triggers
  - rename panels / add clear “monitor-only” label everywhere

Week of 2025-03-31
- Degradation controls PR (redwood#98322) landed behind flag.
- Discussion: load shedding policy
  - Make it tier-aware (free/self-serve shed first)
  - Keep enterprise traffic as stable as possible; don’t oscillate

Week of 2025-04-07
- First prod monitor-only enablement for a limited slice.
- A small real incident occurred later (see Slack #incidents 1715176602): trigger engine recommended DEGRADED but not FAILED.
  - Helpful outcome: gave IC confidence to avoid unnecessary failover.
  - Gap: recommendation didn’t surface “top contributing signals” clearly.

Week of 2025-04-14
- Pre-prod checklist for controlled failover drafted.
- Infra request: explicit change ticket for DNS/edge related toggles even if “we won’t use them.”
- Connor: enforce sign-offs in release runbook (SRE + Platform + Infra).

Week of 2025-04-21 (production controlled failover — low-risk slice)
- Executed progressive failover for low-risk route, free/self-serve only.
- Observations:
  - 5% -> 25% step was smooth; 25% -> 50% caused a transient p99 bump in target region (not enough to abort).
  - Queue wait p99 in target spiked briefly; safe-to-failover check should include “queue slope.”
  - Some customer reports of increased latency but minimal hard failures.
- Post-test actions:
  - adjust safe-to-failover gating (queue slope)
  - tighten rollback documentation + automate rollback verification checks

Week of 2025-04-28
- Threshold tuning session (SRE + Routing + Observability)
  - reduce sensitivity of probe-only triggers
  - adjust DEGRADED p99 threshold for low-traffic periods (avoid triggering on low-volume noise)
  - align paging alerts with burn-rate rather than raw 5xx (still keep raw 5xx as signal input)

Week of 2025-05-05
- Updated notes for exec readout (Neha):
  - We can now detect “regional impairment” earlier and have an auditable decision trail.
  - Biggest remaining risk: capacity estimation under failover load and cross-region network variance.
- Next steps:
  - Expand to additional routes/models
  - Add explicit customer-tier dashboards + customer impact summaries
  - Train on-call rotation (Tomáš scheduling walkthrough)

Action items (rolling)
- [Rafael] Ensure ENG-2842 (signal contract) is reflected in telemetry naming + validation checks.
- [Miles] Document “state machine invariants” (e.g., cannot progress stages if safe-to-failover fails).
- [Aisha] Finalize paging vs warning policy; update multi-region SLO page accordingly.
- [Sergio/Felix] Add “top signals” explainer panel + linkouts to raw metrics.
- [Irene/Victor] Confirm DNS TTL guidance for prod vs test, and add to runbook.
- [Connor] Finalize release gating checklist (sign-offs, rollback, comms).

Notes to self / misc
- Keep reminding folks: the success metric is reduced customer-visible impact + reduced time-to-mitigation; not “we failed over fast.”
- In retro: collect examples of “good non-failover decisions” enabled by better signals.
- We should add a canned Slack/incident-bot message that includes:
  - region state
  - whether monitor-only
  - recommendation
  - safe-to-failover status
  - next suggested action + runbook link
